# PRD: WhatsApp Assistant for Residents

## Problem Statement

Residents miss estate information and reminders because they live on WhatsApp, not on the estate's web surfaces. Exco needs a channel where they can actually reach residents, and residents increasingly expect to transact and check things in chat rather than in a portal. Financially, arrears go uncollected because reminders land in inboxes nobody opens. When a resident does want to know their financial standing, they must call or email the exco — no self-serve path exists.

## Solution

A dedicated WhatsApp Business number operates the estate's **WhatsApp Assistant**: it proactively delivers approved estate information (invoice reminders, payment confirmations, announcements) and, on demand, lets eligible residents peruse their financial standing through a structured menu — balance, last payment, statement, next due, and wallet — in private one-to-one chat, gated by opt-in and an optional PIN.

## User Stories

1. As an eligible resident, I want to message the estate's WhatsApp number and be recognized from my registered phone number, so that I can start using the Assistant without any setup.
2. As an eligible resident with an unrecognized number, I want to link my number via a one-time PIN, so that I can use the Assistant from a phone number not on file.
3. As an eligible resident, I want to consent to WhatsApp alerts during linking, so that I only receive estate broadcasts if I opted in.
4. As a billable resident, I want to see my balance (outstanding across open invoices with an arrears flag), so that I know what I owe at a glance.
5. As a billable resident, I want to see my last payment (amount, date, what it covered), so that I can confirm receipts quickly.
6. As a billable resident, I want to view my statement for a fixed period (this month / this year / last six months), so that I can review my full ledger.
7. As a billable resident, I want to see my next due invoice (amount, due date, line items), so that I can plan payments.
8. As a billable resident, I want to see my wallet balance, so that I know my prepaid position.
9. As a resident holding billable roles on multiple houses, I want to pick which property a financial answer refers to, so that I get per-property truth rather than a mixed answer.
10. As a multi-house resident, I want an all-properties aggregation for my statement, so that I can see my consolidated position in one view.
11. As a resident who opted in, I want my set PIN to gate financial answers, so that a lost or borrowed phone can't read my financial position.
12. As a resident without a PIN, I want financial answers to still work and a gentle nudge offering to set a PIN, so that low-friction access is preserved for non-technical residents.
13. As a resident with a billable role who has NOT opted in, I want identity and consent flow to work but financial answers withheld until I consent, so that the estate stays WhatsApp-compliant.
14. As a resident with a non-billable role (household member, caretaker, staff, contractor), I want estate information (announcements, notices, security updates) but no financial answers, so that I get community value without ledger exposure.
15. As an opted-in resident, I want to text STOP to unsubscribe from broadcasts and START to re-subscribe, so that I control the channel.
16. As an unrostered person, I want a guarded intro that offers onboarding or STOP, so that I'm neither turned away abruptly nor able to guess financial data.
17. As a resident, I want my financial answers to arrive as deterministic menu replies, so that answers are predictable and readable on WhatsApp.
18. As a resident, I want a short PIN-link flow and a 15-minute conversation session, so that interrupted queries resume rather than restarting.
19. As a resident, I want the Assistant to never expose another resident's financial data, so that privacy is preserved in a shared-chat environment.
20. As exco, I want the estate's WhatsApp number to send approved invoice reminders, so that collections improve.
21. As exco, I want a payment-received confirmation on WhatsApp, so that residents see receipts immediately.
22. As exco, I want announcements mirrored to WhatsApp, so that estate news reaches residents where they live.
23. As exco, I want all proactive WhatsApp messages to use pre-approved Meta templates, so that the channel stays compliant.
24. As exco, I want an operational console to view the opt-in registry and bulk-import launch consent, so that I can onboard residents efficiently.
25. As exco, I want a force-PIN toggle, so that I can require PINs estate-wide if security posture tightens.
26. As exco, I want a disclosure-log viewer (searchable by resident/number/date), so that I can audit who saw financial answers.
27. As exco, I want bot health metrics (inbound/outbound counts, delivery failures, template errors), so that I can spot problems early.
28. As exco, I want to inspect and reset stuck sessions, so that a bot loop doesn't wedge a resident.
29. As exco, I want a pending-contacts view, so that I can attach unclaimed numbers to residents.
30. As exco, I want software outbound/lookup caps in system settings, so that a defect can't cause bill shock or a broadcast storm.
31. As an admin, I want every admin write action on the WhatsApp module to require permission and be audited, so that the module follows the estate's security contract.
32. As a developer, I want a WhatsApp simulator harness, so that I can develop the menu without live Meta traffic.
33. As exco, I want a pilot phase (exco/one street) before estate-wide enablement, so that the module is proven on a small base first.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Guardrail exception (ADR-0001):** the WhatsApp Assistant is a deliberate resident-facing surface despite the admin-first guardrail; the web portal remains out of scope.
- **Channel shape (ADR-0002):** Meta WhatsApp Cloud API directly, provider-agnostic behind `src/lib/whatsapp/`; no BSP.
- **Dedicated 1:1 number:** a separate WhatsApp Business number; the existing organic group is untouched.
- **Outbound seam:** implement `sendViaWhatsApp` in the existing notification dispatcher (`src/lib/notifications/send.ts`) and add `whatsapp` to `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS`. All existing producers (invoice reminders, announcements, payment events, queue, history, preferences) are reused unchanged. Note: SMS is currently listed in `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` but is NOT actually implemented — correct this discrepancy (either implement or remove) while touching this file.
- **Inbound seam:** single new module `src/lib/whatsapp/`. Public API: `sendWhatsAppMessage()` (used by the dispatcher stub) and `handleInboundMessage()` (called by the webhook route). Everything conversational lives inside: identity resolution, opt-in/PIN gates, menu engine, session, dedup, disclosure logging. Provider SDK and the `/api/whatsapp/webhook` route stay thin.
- **Webhook:** new Next.js route `/api/whatsapp/webhook`; verify Meta `X-Hub-Signature-256` with the app secret; support the `hub.challenge` handshake. A server route (not a server action) — the mandatory permission/audit contract applies to admin write actions, not the inbound handler.
- **Identity resolution:** match inbound number against `phone_primary` / `phone_secondary`; PIN-link flow as fallback for unrostered numbers; unclaimed numbers become pending contacts surfaced in the console.
- **Access model:** identity open to all; financial disclosure gated on opt-in + PIN-if-set; community tier (announcements/notices) for non-billable roles; financial answers only for billable roles.
- **Menu (v1):** Balance, Last payment, Statement, Next due, Wallet. Statement: fixed periods (this month / this year / last six months) with a rolling cap; property-selection step for multi-house residents; optional all-properties aggregation for statements.
- **PIN:** optional per resident; stored hashed; admin force-PIN toggle as a system setting; PIN-less residents get a one-line nudge.
- **Opt-in:** in-chat capture during PIN-link; `whatsapp_optins` registry; STOP/START self-serve; admin bulk-import for launch.
- **Outbound content (v1):** 3 Meta-approved templates — `invoice_reminder`, `payment_received`, `announcement`. Ad-hoc admin blast is post-v1 once templates exist.
- **State & retention:** `whatsapp_sessions` (15-min TTL), `whatsapp_processed_messages` (dedup via wamid, ~24h window), disclosure log (permanent, immutable, entity type `whatsapp_assistant`), pending contacts. Operational state ephemeral; audit permanent.
- **Admin console:** opt-in registry + bulk import, force-PIN toggle, disclosure-log viewer, bot health, session inspector, pending contacts. Admin writes follow `authorizePermission` + `logAudit`; new permission constants; `AuditEntityType` extended.
- **Cost/limits:** per-conversation costs; outbound burst cap + daily lookup cap in `system_settings`.
- **Rollout:** WhatsApp simulator harness in dev → pilot (exco/one street) → estate-wide toggle.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests assert external behavior through the module's two public entry points (`sendWhatsAppMessage`, `handleInboundMessage`): given an inbound message, the expected reply/state transition occurs — not implementation details of the menu internals.
- **Module tested:** `src/lib/whatsapp/` — identity resolution, opt-in/PIN gating, menu routing, statement composition (fixed periods, property selection, all-properties), session advance/idempotency, dedup, disclosure-log writes, STOP/START, unrostered handling.
- **Dispatcher:** `src/lib/notifications/send.ts` — WhatsApp channel dispatches through `sendViaWhatsApp` when `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` includes `whatsapp`.
- **Admin writes:** module-integration test coverage for new write actions (permission + audit present), following the existing `module-integration.test.ts` pattern with allowlist entries.
- **Prior art:** `src/lib/notifications/__tests__/admin-notifier.test.ts` (unit tests over a notification lib), `src/__tests__/integration/module-integration.test.ts` (structural server-action compliance). E2E harness uses the existing `e2e/` Playwright setup; the WhatsApp simulator replaces live Meta traffic in automated runs.

## Out of Scope

- Ad-hoc admin broadcast composer (post-template add-on).
- Free-text/NLU conversation parsing; LLM assistant.
- Resident web-portal changes (guardrail intact).
- SMS implementation (listed-but-dormant channel; only the `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` discrepancy is fixed here).
- Group-chat integration with the existing WhatsApp group.
- Payment initiation inside the chat (view-only; payments remain on existing paths).
- i18n/localization beyond initial template copy.

## Further Notes

- All proactive messages require pre-approved Meta templates; variable fills go through placeholders. Template copy needs an exco sign-off pass before Meta approval.
- SMS is recorded in `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` but not implemented — resolve this contradiction during the outbound work.
- Financial answers over WhatsApp are not end-to-end encrypted; the PIN layer and disclosure log are the mitigations, and this trade-off is deliberate (ADR-0002 context).
- `CONTEXT.md` glossary defines the canonical terms used here (WhatsApp Assistant, WhatsApp Opt-in, Financial Standing, Billable Role, Eligible Resident, Property Selection, Statement, Community Tier, WhatsApp Session, Disclosure Log, Pending Contact, WhatsApp Template).

Create the provider boundary and verified Meta WhatsApp Cloud API channel for the WhatsApp Assistant. - [ ] Multi-house Residents receive a Property Selection step, while single-house Residents do not; selected property scope is respected in every answer.

- [ ] Each sent financial answer creates an immutable Disclosure Log record with resident, number, property scope, item, timestamp, and PIN-authentication state.
- [ ] Answers use existing authoritative invoice, payment, and wallet data paths and never expose another Resident's data.
- [ ] Tests cover all four queries, opt-in/eligibility/PIN gates, single- and multi-house flows, session expiry, force-PIN, disclosure logging, and authorization failures.

## Parent

P0 Performance track — ACTIONPLAN.md Phase 6.

## What to build

Audit every `useQuery` hook across the codebase and ensure each has a domain-appropriate `staleTime` value. The polling constants in `src/lib/config/polling.ts` define tiers: FAST (5s), REALTIME (30s), STANDARD (60s), SLOW (3min), BACKGROUND (5min). Apply these consistently:

- List/table data: 30-60s (STANDARD range)
- Config/settings/reference data: 5min (BACKGROUND)
- Dashboard aggregated data: 5min (BACKGROUND)
- Real-time data (notifications, status): 5-30s (FAST-REALTIME)

A preliminary audit found `staleTime` already configured across most hooks. Focus the remaining work on:
- Raising the dashboard hook from `REALTIME` (30s) to `BACKGROUND` (5min) since its data is aggregated and stable
- Verifying no hook is missing `staleTime` entirely
- Adding a `staleTime` to any new hooks added by other issues in this performance track

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `useQuery` hook in `src/hooks` has an explicit `staleTime` configured
- [ ] Dashboard hooks use `BACKGROUND` (5min) staleTime
- [ ] List/table hooks use `STANDARD` range (30-60s)
- [ ] Config/reference hooks use `BACKGROUND` (5min)
- [ ] Real-time hooks (notifications, impersonation status) keep FAST-REALTIME range

## Parent

Critique of `/residents/[id]` detail page (Impeccable critique, 2026-08-11).

## What to build

Replace two destructive-data-loss paths on the resident detail page with proper guardrails:

1. **Archive button** currently uses browser-native `confirm()` — replace with the same AlertDialog pattern used for status changes. The dialog must show operational consequences (linked houses, active payments, notes) before confirming. Use "Archive Resident" as the action button text, not a generic "OK".

2. **Resident form** silently clears corporate fields (company_name, rc_number, liaison_contact_name, liaison_contact_phone) via `useEffect` when entity_type toggles away from "corporate". Preserve the values in form state and only clear on explicit form submission, or add a warning dialog before clearing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Archive button opens an AlertDialog (not browser confirm()) showing a summary of what will be affected
- [ ] Archive dialog has a "Cancel" button and a destructive "Archive Resident" button
- [ ] Toggling entity_type from Corporate to Individual in the resident form preserves corporate field values (hidden, not cleared)

content.body:
## Problem Statement

The Residio admin dashboard has a mature invoice, billing, and bank import engine, but lacks two critical financial operational capabilities: (1) bank reconciliation reporting that shows administrators exactly what was imported vs what was matched after each statement upload, and (2) financial period reports with PDF export, scheduled email delivery, and an interactive dashboard replacing the current thin analytics page.

Administrators currently have no way to verify import accuracy at a glance, no PDF exports for statutory reports, and no scheduled report distribution. The existing analytics page is lightweight and does not cover the financial metrics administrators need.

## Solution

**Bank Reconciliation** — After each bank statement import, the import results step displays a reconciliation summary comparing bank totals (credits/debits) to system totals (payments created/expenses created), with unmatched rows flagged for manual review.

**Financial Reports** — The report engine is extended with PDF rendering. Reports can be generated on-demand (PDF download from the Reports page) or scheduled for automatic email delivery with archive storage. A new financial dashboard replaces the existing analytics page, showing revenue/expense trends, collection health, invoice aging by exact-day histogram, and portfolio value.

**Scheduled Delivery** — Reports configured with a schedule are automatically generated, rendered as PDFs, emailed to configured recipients, and archived in the dashboard for re-download by authorized administrators.

## User Stories

1. As an administrator, I want to see a reconciliation summary after each bank statement import so that I can verify every bank transaction was correctly matched to a resident.
2. As an administrator, I want to compare total bank credits against total payments created so that I can catch import discrepancies immediately.
3. As an administrator, I want to see which bank transactions remain unmatched after import processing so that I can manually review them.
4. As an administrator, I want to see unmatched debit transactions flagged for expense category assignment so that I can ensure accurate expense tracking.
5. As a financial secretary, I want to view a financial overview dashboard showing monthly revenue and expense trends so that I can monitor estate financial health.
6. As a financial secretary, I want to see collection health metrics (collection rate, invoice aging, overdue breakdown) so that I can prioritize collection efforts.
7. As a financial secretary, I want an invoice aging histogram showing exact days overdue so that I can identify the worst debtors at a glance.
8. As a financial secretary, I want to see portfolio value (bank balance + petty cash) on the dashboard so that I have a complete picture of estate finances.
9. As an administrator, I want to generate PDF reports for financial overview, collection, and invoice aging so that I can share them with stakeholders.
10. As an administrator, I want to generate PDF reports for debtors, indebtedness, development levy, and transaction logs so that I have reference documents for meetings.
11. As an administrator, I want to schedule reports to generate and email automatically on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis so that I don't need to manually generate routine reports.
12. As an administrator, I want scheduled reports stored in an archive accessible from the Reports page so that I can re-download previously generated reports.
13. As an administrator, I want to see version history for scheduled reports so that I can track what was sent and when.
14. As a chairman, I want the financial dashboard to replace the old analytics page so that the primary analytics surface is financial rather than search/miscellaneous metrics.

## Implementation Decisions

### Bank Reconciliation Summary
- Appears in the import results step, after processing completes (not a separate page).
- Displays a comparison table: bank credits total vs payments created, bank debits total vs expenses created, unmatched rows count.
- Unmatched rows are flagged with a direct link back to the review step for manual matching.
- Implementation hooks into the existing `processImport` results return structure. No new database tables required.

### Financial Dashboard
- Replaces the existing `/analytics` page entirely. Non-financial analytics (search, announcements) are deprecated.
- Dashboard sections: Revenue/Expense Trends (monthly bar/line chart), Collection Health (rate, aging brackets, top debtors), Invoice Aging (bracket summary cards + exact-day histogram), Portfolio Value card.
- Uses the existing recharts library (already installed and lazy-loaded in the analytics page-client pattern).
- Follows the existing analytics page-client pattern with `next/dynamic` lazy-loading and Suspense boundaries per section.

### Report PDF Generation
- Extends the existing report engine (`generateReport`) with a `format` parameter. When `format='pdf'`, the engine returns a PDF buffer alongside the structured data.
- PDF rendering uses `@react-pdf/renderer`, following the existing statement PDF pattern in `src/lib/pdf/account-statement.tsx`.
- Each report type has a dedicated PDF template component.
- Reports generated as PDFs are stored in a new `report_archive` table.

### Report Schedule Delivery
- Extends the existing `report-schedules.ts` to add a `processDueSchedules` function that finds schedules with `next_run_at <= now`, generates PDFs, emails recipients, archives the PDF, and updates `next_run_at`.
- Called by a new cron endpoint: `GET /api/cron/process-report-schedules`.
- Email delivery uses the existing Resend integration via `src/lib/email/send-email.ts`.
- Scheduled PDFs are stored in the `report_archive` table with `schedule_id` linking back to the schedule.

### Report Archive
- New `report_archive` table: `id`, `report_type`, `schedule_id` (nullable, null for on-demand generation), `generated_at`, `generated_by` (user who triggered), `recipients` (JSON array), `file_path` (storage bucket path), `file_size_bytes`, `format` (always 'pdf' initially).
- PDFs stored in a new Supabase storage bucket `report-pdfs` with RLS allowing read for users with `reports.view_financial` permission.
- Archive page accessible from the Reports page with re-download capability.

### Route Changes
- `/analytics` route now renders the new financial dashboard instead of the old analytics page.
- Old analytics components (search analytics, announcement analytics) are removed from the primary analytics route. Revenue trend charts used by the financial dashboard replace them.
- New `/api/cron/process-report-schedules` endpoint registered in `vercel.json`.

### Authorization
- Report generation, scheduling, and archive access require `REPORTS_VIEW_FINANCIAL` permission.
- Report schedule management requires `REPORTS_EXPORT` permission.
- PDF download from archive requires `REPORTS_VIEW_FINANCIAL` permission.
- All new server actions follow the `authorizePermission(PERMISSIONS.X)` + `logAudit()` contract.

## Testing Decisions

- Import reconciliation: unit test the reconciliation structure returned by the processing pipeline. Prior art: `process-email-import.test.ts`.
- Report engine PDF: integration test that calls `generateReport({ type, format: 'pdf' })` and asserts the returned buffer is a valid PDF containing expected data. Prior art: existing report engine in `report-engine.ts` (no existing tests, but the engine structure supports testing).
- Report schedule delivery: unit test `processDueSchedules` by mocking the email sender and storage uploader, asserting schedules are marked as executed. Prior art: `admin-notifier.test.ts`.
- Financial dashboard: component tests for each dashboard section rendering with mock data. Prior art: existing analytics tests pattern if they exist; otherwise standard component-level testing.
- Good tests verify external behavior (PDF structure contains expected content, not pixel-perfect rendering; schedule delivery sends to correct recipients; dashboard displays correct metric values).

## Out of Scope

- Legacy data import (135+ reviewed records) — deferred to a separate phase.
- WhatsApp delivery for scheduled reports — planned for future iteration, not this phase.
- Non-financial analytics (search analytics, announcement analytics) migration — these are deprecated from the analytics page but not migrated to new surfaces.
- Payment gateway integration — explicitly deferred per project roadmap.
- Invoice dispute system — existing disputes only log to audit; no new dispute table or workflow.
- SMS delivery — not operational, not part of this phase.

## Further Notes

- The existing analytics page-client already uses `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false` for recharts components. The new financial dashboard follows this same pattern for consistency.
- The report engine already supports 7 report types. Adding PDF rendering is an output-format extension, not a data-generation change.
- `@react-pdf/renderer` is already a dependency (used by the account statement PDF). No new package dependencies required.
- The existing Resend email integration handles sending; new report delivery code should use the same `sendEmail` function.

## Problem Statement

The current Generate Invoices action on `/billing` provides no preview before execution, no month/scope selection, no wallet/email controls, no resident-targeted billing profiles, and no robust duplicate/concurrency protection. Operators trigger invoice generation blindly against the current month without knowing what will be created, what wallets will be deducted, or what emails will be sent.

## Solution

A phased enhancement to the invoice generation pipeline adding:
1. Dry-run preview with target-month and scope selection
2. Explicit wallet/email side-effect controls
3. Resident-targeted billing profile support
4. Database-level duplicate/concurrency protection
5. Run history with downloadable results and retry support

## User Stories

1. As an administrator, I want to preview invoice generation before executing so that I can review what will be created before committing.
2. As a financial secretary, I want to choose the billing month and scope (house, street, resident) so that I can target specific billing runs.
3. As an administrator, I want to decide whether wallet deductions and emails fire during generation so that historical backfills don't trigger unintended notifications.
4. As an administrator, I want resident-targeted billing profiles to generate invoices against their configured roles so that individual resident charges are automated.
5. As an administrator, I want duplicate generation to be impossible so that re-running a period doesn't create duplicate invoices or wallet deductions.
6. As an administrator, I want failed runs to expose actionable details and be safely retryable so that I can recover from errors.
7. As a financial secretary, I want to see generation history with downloadable results so that I can audit billing operations.

## Implementation Decisions

- Preview uses the existing `generateMonthlyInvoices` engine but wraps it in a read-only mode: queries data, computes what would happen, returns structured preview without writing.
- Month selector and scope filters (house, street, resident) are passed as parameters to the preview and execution endpoints.
- Wallet debit and email delivery become boolean flags on the execution request, defaulting off for historical backfills.
- Resident-targeted profiles are processed in a separate pass that matches residents to profiles by applicable roles and validates overlap.
- Database uniqueness constraint on (resident_id, house_id, billing_profile_id, period_start, period_end) for invoices.
- `invoice_generation_log` table is already present and captures run metadata; it is extended with the new fields.

## Testing Decisions

- Preview: unit test that a dry-run returns expected invoice counts without writing.
- Execution: integration test that flags (wallet, email) are respected.
- Resident-targeted: unit test that role-matching produces correct resident assignments.
- Concurrency: integration test that duplicate runs are blocked.

## Out of Scope

- Payment gateway integration
- Legacy data import
- Statement generation (covered by separate PRD #24)

Add database-level protection against duplicate invoices and concurrent generation runs.

Discovered during Analytics dashboard data validation (see SESSION_STATE.md 2026-08-15 entry). The Top 10 Indebted/Non-Indebted widget on `/analytics?tab=collections` only ever shows 6 residents because only 6 of 193 residents (139 of whom are billable — 120 tenants + 19 resident-landlords) have ever had an invoice generated.

## Root cause (confirmed via live queries against the cloud DB)

- **Not a missing billing-profile issue**: all 178 active houses already have `billing_profile_id` set directly. `house_types.billing_profile_id` is unused/null everywhere, but that column isn't what generation reads from.
- **All 581 existing invoices were created within a 2-day window (2026-08-09 to 2026-08-10)** — a one-time bulk backfill / test-data seed, not output from the recurring monthly cron accumulating history over time. ## Problem Statement

The Personnel & Vendors directory lists active staff, contractors, vendors, and suppliers without showing who is accountable for each working relationship. Estate administrators cannot tell whether a person works for the Estate or for a particular Resident House, cannot see house-specific responsibility, and cannot preserve accountability history when work changes.

## Solution

Add dated Personnel Engagements. Each engagement makes either the Estate or a Resident House accountable for a Personnel record. Personnel can hold several concurrent engagements, but only one active engagement for each accountability target. Ending an engagement preserves history without changing the directory-wide Personnel status.

The Personnel directory surfaces compact active-accountability badges and filters. The existing Add/Edit Personnel dialog manages repeatable Estate and Resident-House engagements, including an optional context-specific responsibility and start/end dates.

## User Stories

1. As an estate administrator, I want to assign estate-employed Personnel to the Estate so that estate security, facilities, and administrative staff have a clear accountable party.
2. As an estate administrator, I want to assign Personnel to an active Resident House so that domestic staff, private drivers, gardeners, and house-specific contractors are traceable to the resident responsible for them.
3. As an estate administrator, I want to record an engagement-specific responsibility so that a person's general job title and their duty for a particular accountable party are distinguishable.
4. As an estate administrator, I want one Personnel record to have several active engagements so that shared workers and contractors can be accountable to several Resident Houses or to both the Estate and a Resident House.
5. As an estate administrator, I want the system to prevent duplicate active engagements for the same Personnel and accountability target so that accountability is unambiguous.
6. As an estate administrator, I want to create Resident-House Engagements only from active Resident Houses so that I cannot assign new responsibility to stale occupancy.
7. As an estate administrator, I want an ended Resident-House Engagement to remain visible after that Resident House becomes inactive so that the accountability history stays defensible.
8. As an estate administrator, I want to end one engagement without changing the Personnel status so that a person who continues working elsewhere remains Active.
9. As an estate administrator, I want existing Personnel with no engagement to show as Unassigned so that I can work through missing accountability data without the system making assumptions.
10. As an estate administrator, I want to filter the directory by Estate, Resident-House, and Unassigned accountability so that I can find the people for whom I am responsible.
11. As an estate administrator, I want the directory to show the first active accountability target and a count of additional targets so that I can scan the directory without losing multi-engagement context.
12. As an estate administrator, I want to open a Personnel record and see the full dated engagement history so that I can investigate responsibility during an incident or payment review.
13. As an estate administrator, I want to update the general Personnel job title without overwriting engagement-specific responsibility so that profile data remains reusable across engagements.
14. As an authorized administrator, I want all Personnel Engagement writes audited so that changes to estate and resident accountability are traceable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Add a Personnel Engagement persistence model linked to the existing Personnel-backed `vendors` table.
- An engagement has exactly one accountability scope: Estate or Resident House.
- A Resident-House Engagement references the existing Resident House relationship, rather than a House alone, because accountability must identify both the house and the responsible resident.
- The Estate scope has no Resident House reference. A Resident-House scope requires one.
- Every Personnel type can receive either engagement scope.
- The general Personnel `job_title` remains profile-level. An engagement may carry an optional engagement-specific responsibility.
- Engagements record a start date and optional end date. Ending an engagement preserves the record as history; it is never overwritten or deleted as a substitute for history.
- A new Resident-House Engagement is permitted only when its Resident House is active. Historical engagements remain readable even after that Resident House ends.
- Enforce one active engagement for the same Personnel and accountability target at the database level, alongside application validation.
- Personnel status remains directory-wide. An individual engagement ending does not make Personnel Inactive or Terminated.
- Existing Personnel receive no inferred engagement. They display as Unassigned until an administrator creates an engagement.
- Extend Personnel read models to include active engagement summaries and full engagement history for the editor.
- Extend the directory with an Accountability column and filter. An active Estate Engagement displays `Estate`; an active Resident-House Engagement displays the house and responsible resident; multiple targets display the first target plus an additional count.
- Extend the existing Add/Edit Personnel dialog with a repeatable Engagements section. It supports adding Estate and Resident-House engagements, responsibility, start/end dates, and ending an active engagement.
- New write actions use the existing Personnel management permission and audit integration convention.

## Testing Decisions

- Test externally visible behavior through Personnel engagement actions and the directory query model, not individual implementation helpers or table markup.
- Test valid Estate and Resident-House engagement creation, rejection of inactive Resident Houses, rejection of duplicate active targets, and preserved Personnel status/history after ending one engagement.
- Test directory query summaries and Estate, Resident-House, and Unassigned filter behavior.
- Add dialog behavior coverage for adding both scopes, validation feedback, and ending an existing engagement.
- Add the new write actions to the module-integration compliance coverage for permission checks and audit logging.

## Out of Scope

- A dedicated Personnel detail page.
- Personnel-to-Personnel or company/subcontractor accountability relationships.
- Inferring Estate responsibility for existing Personnel.
- Payroll, wage, contract, access-control, or expense-allocation workflows.
- Changing the general Personnel type or status lifecycle.

## Further Notes

- Canonical domain vocabulary is documented in `CONTEXT.md`: Personnel Engagement, Estate Engagement, Resident-House Engagement, Personnel Status, and Unassigned Personnel.
- This is an admin-dashboard feature. No Resident Portal work is included.

- Non-admin/unauthorized callers cannot retrieve another resident's invoice data via the `resident_id` param.
- Per CLAUDE.md module integration requirements: add/confirm the relevant permission constants in `src/lib/auth/action-roles.ts` if not already covered by an existing `BILLING_VIEW`-equivalent permission.
